Fit a phylogenetic Gaussian-process model

Source: R/fit.R
phylo_gp.Rd

Fits y ~ N(X beta, K) where K is the covariance implied by kernel on tree. The Stan program is written by kernel_stancode(), compiled once (and cached), and run with cmdstanr.

Usage

phylo_gp(
  formula,
  data,
  tree,
  kernel,
  method = c("sample", "optimize"),
  species = NULL,
  se = NULL,
  prior_sigma_scale = NULL,
  prior_beta_scale = NULL,
  chains = 4,
  iter_warmup = 1000,
  iter_sampling = 1000,
  adapt_delta = 0.9,
  seed = 1,
  n_starts = 8,
  ...
)

Arguments

formula

Model formula, e.g. brain ~ body.

data

Data frame. Species are matched to tip labels through species or, if species is NULL, the row names. With species, a species may have several rows (repeated measurements); see Details.

tree

A phylo tree with branch lengths.

kernel

A kernel, e.g. k_bm() + k_white().

method

"sample" (Bayesian, HMC) or "optimize" (maximum likelihood: no priors, no Jacobian, several starts). Kernels with latent rates (k_relaxed(), k_rate_time()) need "sample".

species

Optional name of the column of data holding species names. Needed when species have several rows.

se

Optional name of a column with known measurement-error standard deviations.

prior_sigma_scale, prior_beta_scale

Prior scales; see kernel_standata().

chains, iter_warmup, iter_sampling, adapt_delta, seed

Passed to cmdstanr's $sample().

n_starts

Number of optimisation starts for method = "optimize".

...

Further arguments to $sample() or $optimize().

Value

An object of class phylogp_fit.

Details

Several rows per species. When some species have more than one row, the model is $$y_{ij} = x_{ij}^\top\beta + f_i + \epsilon_{ij}, \quad \epsilon_{ij} \sim N(0, \sigma_w^2),$$ where \(f\) is the Gaussian process given by kernel over species and \(\sigma_w\) (within_sigma) is the residual standard deviation within species. A k_white() component is then the non-phylogenetic species effect (the (1 | species) term of a mixed model). The likelihood is exact and keeps its linear cost: it factorises into the species means, which follow the kernel with an extra tip variance \(\sigma_w^2/n_i\), and the deviations from those means. Predictors may vary within species. Leave-one-out leaves out whole species. Not yet available with varying slopes or known measurement error (se).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
tr <- ape::rcoal(50)
d <- data.frame(y = kernel_simulate(k_bm() + k_white(), tr)[, 1])
fit <- phylo_gp(y ~ 1, d, tr, k_bm() + k_white())
fit
loo(fit)
} # }
